title: Hypothesis-Weighted Prioritization for Traffic-Shaped Roadmaps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: introduce a prioritization framework that blends traditional RICE elements with hypothesis-driven traffic shaping signals to better surface initiatives that materially improve production unit economics and user-facing latency in the short-to-medium term.

Overview: The Hypothesis-Weighted Prioritization (HWP) framework replaces a single static Confidence modifier with an evidence-backed Hypothesis score and introduces an explicit Traffic Impact dimension. The goal is to rank initiatives by expected net latency-cost benefit where hypotheses are actively validated during the cycle.

Core scoring formula (human-readable):
  HWP Score = (Impact * HypothesisStrength * Urgency) / (EstimatedCost + OperationalRiskFactor) * TrafficWeight

Where:
  - Impact: user/business value on a 1-10 scale (like RICE Reach*Effectiveness aggregated).
  - HypothesisStrength: 0.2-1.2 multiplier based on validation tier (0.2 = pure idea, 1.0 = validated A/B signal, 1.2 = replicated customer telemetry).
  - Urgency: 1-3 urgency multiplier tied to OKR timelines and external dependencies.
  - EstimatedCost: normalized cost units (expected token/GPU ops + infra changes).
  - OperationalRiskFactor: penalty 0-2 for rollout risk, backward compatibility, security review overhead.
  - TrafficWeight: 0.5-2 multiplier emphasizing initiatives that affect high-traffic paths (derived from request volume percent and SLO breach exposure).

Validation lifecycle: every initiative must supply a short hypothesis (what will change and why), an observable metric to validate (latency p95, cost per 1M tokens, availability), and a quick validation plan (canary, synthetic test, pilot). HypothesisStrength is updated mid-cycle based on preliminary telemetry.

Trade-offs and design decisions made so far:
  - Chose HypothesisStrength vs. Confidence to encourage active experiments rather than static guesses. Trade-off: extra process overhead for PMs/ENG to supply validation plans.
  - TrafficWeight ensures small infra changes that touch hot paths surface higher. Risk: may deprioritize high-value low-traffic features — we mitigate with an override field for strategic bets.
  - OperationalRiskFactor captures non-cost blockers (compliance, migrations). We debated encoding it within Cost but split for decision clarity.

Artifacts and links:
  - Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Roadmap/pages/HWP-PRD
  - Example dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/roadmap/hwp-examples
  - Figma prioritization board: https://www.figma.com/file/hwp-board
  - Prototype spreadsheet with scoring templates: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/HWP-template
  - Related GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap-framework/pulls/214

Acceptance criteria:
  - Framework doc approved by Product Leadership and one Eng lead.
  - Scoring template populated for top 30 initiatives and scores calculated.
  - Two in-flight initiatives with hypothesis plans and canary validation configured in Sandbox.

Risks: additional PM/Eng time to produce validation plans; potential gaming of HypothesisStrength. Mitigations: require telemetry sources, tie HypothesisStrength to verifiable metrics, quarterly audit of scored initiatives.
